I would have to say this, Mr. Wallace,
we are terribly imaginative as far technique and science is concerned.
As far changes in social arrangements are concerned,
we lack utterly in imagination.
If we would have...
But Dr. Fromm, I keep thinking as you talk,
we have been told that we, by certain persons,
that we have a creeping socialism now going on in the United States,
and certainly it is a more socialistic country today
than it was, let's say, twenty or twenty-five years ago.
And yet, you yourself complain about bureaucracy.
You yourself complain that the individual is losing his way
in this state in which we live,
and at the same time you call for more socialism.
Aren't you just adding poison to the poison
that is already being injected into our systems,
if indeed socialism be poison?
Yes, but what is...
Well, for me socialism is exactly the opposite
of a bureaucratically managed culture.
We talk a great deal about Russia today,
and I'm afraid that in twenty years
we and Russia will be more similar than different.
Why?
Because what is common to both societies
is the development into a managed mass society
with big bureaucracies, managing people.
The Russians do it by force, we do it by persuasion.
I appreciate the tremendous difference
that we can express ideas without being afraid of being killed or imprisoned.
But I think the Russians might do away with the terror
in twenty or thirty years when they are richer
and when they don't need these repressive methods so much.
What we have in common is a mass man, a mass bureaucracy,
and a manipulation of everyone to act smoothly,
but with the illusion that he follows his own decisions and opinions.
So far, I personally, if I may express an opinion, go with you.
But I find it difficult to go with your solution.
I go with your diagnosis, but not to your cure,
because I don't understand your socialism, I guess.
Well, you see, that is so difficult
because the Russians have succeeded in one thing.
They have sold the world the idea
that they represent socialism and the ideas of Marx.
And we have done the greatest service to their propaganda
by agreeing that that's what it is.
I would need much more time to explain.
